intro: BBC Sport reports that Premier League chief executive Richard Masters has criticised FIFA president Gianni Infantino's proposal for a World Cup 'sell-off' plan, saying the organisation has "pressed the self-destruct button." The remarks underline growing public tensions between domestic leagues and football's global governing body over proposals that affect international tournaments.

sections.heading: What BBC Sport reported and the core comment
sections.text: According to BBC Sport, Richard Masters — the chief executive of the Premier League — has publicly criticised a plan put forward by FIFA president Gianni Infantino that has been described as a World Cup sell-off. Masters used very strong language, saying FIFA has "pressed the self-destruct button" in response to the proposal. The report captures an escalation in rhetoric from a senior figure in one of Europe's most powerful domestic competitions.

sections.heading: Background: the organisations and personalities involved
sections.text: The Premier League is England's top professional football division and is run by a collective of clubs with a chief executive who represents the league's interests. FIFA is the global governing body that organises international competitions such as the World Cup and is led by its president, Gianni Infantino. Both institutions routinely interact — and sometimes clash — over calendars, player release, commercial rights and the broader structure of international football. Public criticism from a domestic league chief executive towards FIFA's leadership is notable because it highlights friction at the highest level between club football and global governance.

analysis: Masters' language, as reported by BBC Sport, signals a serious disagreement between a leading domestic competition and FIFA leadership. While the exact details of the so-called sell-off plan are not set out in the single-line report excerpt, the choice of words — that FIFA has "pressed the self-destruct button" — suggests that Premier League leadership views the proposal as potentially damaging to the sport's governance, credibility or commercial balance. Analysts might see this as part of a longer-running clash over international calendars and the balance of influence between clubs, leagues and FIFA, where each party is defending competing commercial and sporting interests.

faq.answer: BBC Sport reports that Richard Masters, the Premier League chief executive, criticised FIFA president Gianni Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan and said the organisation had "pressed the self-destruct button."

faq.question: Who are the main people involved in this dispute?
faq.answer: The figures named in the BBC Sport report are Richard Masters, who is the chief executive of the Premier League, and Gianni Infantino, who serves as president of FIFA.

faq.question: What is meant by a 'World Cup sell-off plan'?
faq.answer: The BBC Sport excerpt describes the proposal as a 'sell-off' plan but does not detail its contents. In general terms, the phrase could refer to proposals involving commercial arrangements, rights sales or structural changes to the World Cup; however, the specific meaning or mechanics of the plan in question are not provided in the report excerpt.

conclusion: The BBC Sport report captures a sharp public rebuke from the Premier League's top executive aimed at FIFA leadership over a controversial World Cup proposal. Whatever the full details of the plan, the exchange underlines the persistent and high-stakes tensions that can arise between domestic competitions and football's global governing body.
